notes.text: Quinn Hughes is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin. That pair has had 52% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 67:11 together, about what it had with Hughes (56%).

Olli Määttä is out (upper body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin. That pair has had 48% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 90:20 together, about what it had with Määttä (48%).
Marcus Foligno is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, down from 34% last season.
Danila Yurov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 28 games, up from 6% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 20% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
A.J. Greer is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 13 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Leo Carlsson is on injured reserve and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-six forward.
Beckett Sennecke returned in their last game after missing 3 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Stian Solberg was added to the roster on Nov 21 and has played beside Tristan Luneau.

stakes: The Wild go in first in the NHL with 42 points, the Ducks tied for fourth in the Pacific with 25 points.

story.head: This one’s going to leave marks
paras: The Wild (18-4-6) lost 4-3 in a shootout to Colorado on Friday, and the Ducks (12-14-1) lost 5-3 to Los Angeles the same night. Going in, the Wild are first in the NHL and the Ducks fifth in the Pacific (tied for 22nd in the NHL).

The Wild’s record (.750) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.633), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Ducks have played better than their record (.463) says: their chances are worth about .525, and losses in one-goal games have held them back.

The Wild block more shots than almost anyone (2nd) and draw more penalties than they take (2nd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). Minnesota has allowed 2.29 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. As for the Ducks, they have had shaky goaltending (29th). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (31st), so the Wild keep dangerous shots away, but they give up a lot of them. Anaheim has allowed 3.70 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. Both teams like to hit, especially the Ducks (4th), so expect plenty of it.

Kirill Kaprizov (19 G / 30 A / 49 P in 28 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is second in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games and seven goals in eight games against Anaheim since 2023-24. For the Ducks, Cutter Gauthier (23 G / 9 A / 32 P in 26 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Mikael Granlund (8 G / 23 A / 31 P in 26 GP) is next in line.

Jesper Wallstedt (16-3-5 / .918 SV% in 24 GS) has been a rock in net for Minnesota and will likely start. Anaheim has two options in net: Laurent Brossoit (5-2-0 / .876 SV% in 7 GS) and Lukáš Dostál (4-7-1 / .857 SV% in 13 GS). Brossoit has started four of their last ten games, including the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
